reasons: Only four of the eight sections were available, so the role entries and education data could not be reviewed.

terms.meaning: a written description of the shape data must have, checked before the code runs
a field that may be left out of an entry

depends_on: No imports in the visible sections

sections.name: BattleLink
sections.title: Link shape
sections.what: Describes a labelled web link: a display name and an address.
sections.why: Reused for the links and tools listed under each role.

sections.name: KeyProject
sections.title: Key project shape
sections.what: Describes a headline engagement: its industry, a short description, an optional problem type and optional place keys.
sections.why: Each role's projects are described the same way, so they can be drawn as scenes.
sections.watch_out: Place keys must match the names in the geography data, or the place will not show.

sections.name: Battle
sections.title: Role shape
sections.what: Describes one role: company, title, dates, location, status (current, worked or built), tags, industries, description and optional projects, links, tools, problem statements, frameworks and highlight boxes.
sections.why: One shape feeds the timeline, the Atlas and the brain map.
sections.watch_out: The period field must contain years as text, since dates are read from it.

sections.name: Education
sections.title: Education shape
sections.what: Describes a degree: institution, degree, period, grade and a note.
sections.why: Keeps education in the same typed form as roles.
sections.watch_out: The grade is text, not a number, so comparing grades needs care.

sections.name: battles (part 1)
sections.title: Bain and Aranca career entries
sections.what: Opens the battles list with two career entries: the current Bain & Company role, which covers advisory work and an AI toolkit, and the earlier Aranca growth advisory role. Each entry holds its headline facts, a description, key projects with location tags, and links to the tools built in that role.
sections.why: Likely reason: this file is the single place where career history is written, so other data files can read the same source.
sections.watch_out: Each key project's location tags must match a key in the places list in geo.ts, or that location is silently left off the globe.

sections.name: battles (part 2)
sections.title: Evalueserve, Tecnova and Delbomblr entries
sections.what: Adds three earlier career entries: Evalueserve (competitive intelligence for technology clients), Tecnova India (market entry work), and a short Delbomblr founder's office entry. The Delbomblr entry has fewer fields, with no key projects or tools.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code. The shorter Delbomblr entry simply leaves out the optional fields.
sections.watch_out: Optional fields such as key projects and tools can be missing, so any code that reads them must handle an empty value.

sections.name: battles (part 3)
sections.title: Madcue and Parikshit personal entries
sections.what: Adds two entries that are not paid company roles: Madcue, a media platform the owner co-founded, and Parikshit, a student satellite team where the owner led attitude control. Each gives headline facts, a long description, and links to outside pages or to a page on this site. Part of the Madcue text was cut off in the view used for these notes, so its full wording is not described here.
sections.why: Likely reason: these were built or research work rather than paid roles, so they use different status and section labels to group them apart.
sections.watch_out: The Parikshit publications link points to a path on this site, so renaming that page breaks the link.

sections.name: education
sections.title: University education record
sections.what: Holds the one education record: a B.Tech in Mechanical Engineering from Manipal Institute of Technology, covering 2012 to 2016, with a grade and a short personal note.
sections.why: Likely reason: the education record has a different shape from a career entry, so it is exported on its own.
sections.watch_out: The grade is stored as text, not a number, so it cannot be compared or sorted by value without converting it first.

summary: Defines the shape of a career entry (role, company, dates and projects), plus the shared types for links, key projects and education. Only part of the file was available to review.
purpose: The source for the experience section: each role on the site and its details, which several other files read.
why: Typed fields keep the role data consistent for the Atlas, the home page and the brain map.
how: 1) Defines a link type. 2) Defines a key project with industry, description, problem type and places. 3) Defines a role with dates, status, tags, industries and optional details. 4) Defines an education record. 5) The role entries and education records themselves are in later sections that were not included here.
inputs: Not in this packet for the role entries; they are typed data written in the file.
outputs: Typed role and education lists used by other files.
risks: The status field must be CURRENT, WORKED or BUILT, and a typo fails the type check. Dates are free text, and the Atlas reads years from them, so a bad format breaks placement.
debug: If a role is missing from the Atlas, check its period text includes years. If a type error appears, check that status is one of the three allowed values.
